The generic-interface corpus is generated independently with Windows PowerShell 5 and .NET Framework CLR 4.0.30319.42000. The original Pascal compiler is never invoked. C# and the managed runtime are development-only tools excluded from native installation and portable packages.

Regenerate with:

```powershell
& "$env:SystemRoot\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File native/tests/reference/generate-generic-enumerators.ps1
```

The complete [generator](../reference/generic-enumerators.cs) records 4488 operations over 22 sources: nonempty/empty arrays and strings, List, HashSet, dictionary Keys/Values, integer/character ranges (including empty), Repeat (including empty), Select and Where with and without indices, Iterate, recurrent/indexed SeqGen and SeqWhile. Four rounds use Random(371+round), first a fixed protocol then 28 random operations. Slots are genuine IEnumerator<T> references: aliases share one state, unlike the concrete structs in the separate Dictionary corpus. Fields are case, round, slot, operation and outcome. Character Current is serialized as its integer code; ~ denotes nil. InvalidOperationException from Current maps to E_ITERATOR_STATE; unsupported/not-implemented Reset to E_NOT_SUPPORTED; disposed CharEnumerator errors to E_NIL.

Each row is checked by a separately compiled native Pascal program recreating that source and every earlier successful state-changing operation. Earlier failed operations are omitted because the probes have verified they leave state unchanged; Current reads have no side effects and are also omitted from the prefix. This preserves the reference sequence without adding exception handling to the tested language. Additional tests exercise source mutation, live array Current versus saved List Current, concrete Dictionary boxing/copies/Reset, ref identity and casts, types rejected before output, record values, closures and ownership cycles, file disposal, allocation/work limits, cancellation and malformed bytecode.

Reference contracts: [IEnumerator<T>](https://github.com/microsoft/referencesource/blob/main/mscorlib/system/collections/generic/ienumerator.cs), [array enumerators](https://github.com/microsoft/referencesource/blob/main/mscorlib/system/array.cs), [CharEnumerator](https://github.com/microsoft/referencesource/blob/main/mscorlib/system/charenumerator.cs), [Dictionary](https://github.com/microsoft/referencesource/blob/main/mscorlib/system/collections/generic/dictionary.cs), [legacy LINQ iterators](https://github.com/microsoft/referencesource/blob/main/System.Core/System/Linq/Enumerable.cs), and the local original bin/Lib/PABCSystem.pas for Range/SeqFill/character adapters. In particular, Range and Repeat Dispose are no-ops in the legacy implementation; string Dispose invalidates its source; nonindexed Select/Where clear Current on disposal.

This establishes the implemented closed generic protocol, not a complete interface/type-system or library port. Concrete List/HashSet public enumerator structs and their public identity are now covered separately by collection-enumerators-reference.tsv. Nongeneric IEnumerator/object boxing, variance, arbitrary user implementations/generics, bound method values and CLR-private reflected type names remain separate work. Native sequence implementation tags preserve closed source/provider identities without pretending to load arbitrary managed types. Direct IntRange/CharRange/NewSet GetEnumerator and multiline diagnostic locations are also checked. Simple PABCSystem numeric/Iterate yield loops retain no-op disposal; empty integer Range is adapted to the Empty array contract and its enumerator identity. Before/after Current behavior of additional custom providers beyond the independently covered cases is not claimed as full original compiler compatibility.
